newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on fund short covering.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on fund short covering.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher on Friday on fund short covering tied to signals the market was oversold, pit sources said.
Funds bought at least 10 million bushels, pushing the July contract up 6-3/4 cents.
Commercials were light buyers on the day, keying off of reports soybean and soyoil basis bids in Brazil had firmed.
"It's 100 percent dependent on what goes on with the Brazilian premiums and they were firming this morning," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst with E.D. and F. Man International in Chicago.

Sernatinger said soybean basis levels were at 24 cents under CBOT July futures on Friday, compared with 27 under on Thursday. One cash trader said soyoil bids firmed to 20 under CBOT July, against 50 under on Thursday.

Soybeans had faltered much of the morning on bearish input from the weekly crush. The National Oilseed Processors Association said U.S. soy crushings during the week ended May 14 totaled 23.457 million bushels. The market was expecting a crush pace from 23.6 million to 25.1 million bushels.
Soybeans ended 6-3/4 to 3-3/4 cents per bushel with July up 6-3/4 at $8.64-1/2.

New crop gained on ideas cold weather, while not deadly to developing plants, could slow germination. They noted soil temperatures remained below normal so even early planted soybeans were not benefitting from the quick start.
The May contract spiked near midday as shorts scrambled to get out ahead of expiry on Tuesday. Open interest as of Friday morning was at 8,305 contracts, down 2,610 from the previous session.

On the day, funds bought at least 10 million bushels, led by Refco Inc with three million bushels July and 1.5 million November, traders said. Rosenthal Collins bought three million November and Prudential Securities bought 2.5 million July.
Continental Grain spread 1.5 million November/September at 42 to 43 cents, premium September. Cargill Inc spread one million July/November at $1.48 to $1.50, premium July.
The July/November spread widened by 2-3/4 cents to close at $1.55, premium July.

In options, Prudential Securities was an aggressive buyer of $8.75 calls at premiums from 16-1/2 to 22-1/2 cents. Continental Grain bought 300 July $8.75 calls and sold 300 July $9.75 calls at 15-1/4 to 15-1/2 cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 60,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 59,104 contracts.
